methods.label: Compose the rational functions and bound the modulus
methods.explanation:
First handle the possibility that \(f\) is constant. If \(a=b\), then \(f(z)=1\) wherever it is defined. When \(b\ne-1\), all later iterates also equal \(1\), so they cannot equal every allowed input \(z\). When \(a=b=-1\), however, \(f(z)=1\) for \(z\ne1\), while \(f(1)\) is undefined. Thus \(g\) has empty domain, and the stated identity holds because there are no inputs to check. This allowed case has \(|b|=1\).

Now assume \(a\ne b\). Cross-multiplication shows that \(f(u)=f(v)\) implies \((b-a)(u-v)=0\), so \(f\) is one-to-one on its domain. At each of four successive evaluations, at most one additional starting input can reach the forbidden value \(-b\). Therefore \(g(g(z))\) is defined for infinitely many \(z\), which allows its identity to impose coefficient conditions.

Composing \(f\) with itself gives
\[
g(z)=\frac{(1+a)z+a(1+b)}{(1+b)z+a+b^2}.
\]
For shorter calculations, put
\[
p=1+a,\quad q=a(1+b),\quad
r=1+b,\quad s=a+b^2.
\]
Then, at inputs where the original compositions are defined,
\[
g(g(z))=
\frac{(p^2+qr)z+q(p+s)}{r(p+s)z+rq+s^2}.
\]
Setting this equal to \(z\) and clearing the nonzero denominator yields
\[
r(p+s)z^2+(s^2-p^2)z-q(p+s)=0.
\]
A nonzero polynomial of degree at most two cannot vanish at infinitely many inputs. In particular, its quadratic coefficient must be zero, giving
\[
(1+b)(1+2a+b^2)=0.
\]
Thus either \(b=-1\), which gives \(|b|=1\), or
\[
b^2+1=-2a.
\]
In the second case, \(|a|=1\) implies \(|b^2+1|=2\). Using the triangle inequality and \(|b^2|=|b|^2\), we obtain
\[
2\le |b|^2+1,
\qquad
|b|^2=|(b^2+1)-1|\le2+1.
\]
Hence every allowed case satisfies
\[
1\le |b|\le\sqrt3.
\]

Both endpoints actually occur. Take \(a=1,b=-1\). Then \(g(z)=z\) wherever the original composition is defined, so \(|b|=1\) is possible. For the other endpoint, take \(a=1,b=i\sqrt3\). Here
\[
p=2,\quad s=-2,\quad q=r=1+i\sqrt3.
\]
Thus \(p+s=0\) and \(p^2+qr=2+2i\sqrt3\ne0\). The displayed composition formula therefore reduces to \(g(g(z))=z\) on its original domain, establishing \(|b|=\sqrt3\).

The difference between the largest and smallest values is consequently \(\boxed{\sqrt3-1}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
